 Tax audit deadline ends: What should taxpayers do now?
 Tax audit reports may be accepted after the deadline if taxpayers have sufficient cause for the delay, but late filing can attract penalties and affect certain tax benefits 
 Ayush Mishra 
 October 22, 2026 / 12:50 IST 
 Share -->
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 Representative image 
 Tax audit reports can be filed late under the Income-tax Act.
 Delays may incur penalties unless reasonable cause is proven.
 Ensure audit report details match ITR to avoid tax notices.

 The deadline to file tax audit reports for the financial year 2025-26 ended on October 21, 2026. However, taxpayers who have missed the deadline may still be able to submit their reports, subject to the applicable provisions and consequences of delayed filing. They should also ensure that the information disclosed in the tax audit report matches the details reported in their income-tax return ( ITR ) to avoid discrepancies and possible notices from the Income Tax Department.
 Can taxpayers file tax audit reports after the deadline? 
Mihir Tanna, Associate Director at SK Patodia LLP, said the Income-tax Act does not prohibit filing a tax audit report after the due date. However, a delay can attract penalties and may affect certain tax benefits.
 “The requirement to file the audit report before the return of income is directory rather than mandatory,” Tanna said, adding that a report may be accepted at a later stage if there is sufficient cause for the delay.
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 The procedure for submitting the report remains the same, whether it is filed before or after the deadline. However, taxpayers should not assume that a delayed submission will automatically be accepted without consequences.
 What penalty can apply for missing the deadline? 
Under Section 271B of the Income-tax Act, a taxpayer who fails to get accounts audited or furnish the audit report as required may face a penalty of 0.5 percent of total sales, turnover or gross receipts, subject to a maximum of Rs 1.5 lakh.
 However, the penalty is not automatic. Tanna said no penalty should be imposed if the taxpayer can establish that there was a reasonable cause for the delay.
 Examples include a delay in the appointment of an auditor by the approving authority or the seizure of books of account by government authorities, which prevents the audit from being completed on time. 
Taxpayers who have missed the deadline should therefore complete the audit and submit the report as soon as possible, while retaining documents that explain the reasons for the delay.
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 Avoid mismatches between the tax audit report and ITR 
Filing the tax audit report is only one part of the compliance process. Taxpayers must ensure that the figures and disclosures in the report, particularly Form 3CD, are consistent with those in the ITR. The ITR filing deadline for audit related cases is November 21, 2026.
 Suresh Surana, a Mumbai-based chartered accountant, said mismatches between the tax audit report and ITR can trigger notices, defective return alerts or scrutiny by the Income Tax Department.

 Common errors include differences in turnover, net profit and balance sheet figures, failure to add back inadmissible expenses, incorrect reporting of brought-forward losses or unabsorbed depreciation, and omission of income or tax adjustments disclosed by the auditor.
 Taxpayers should also select the correct ITR form and ensure that the audit report's acknowledgement number, filing date and form details are correctly reported.
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 What should taxpayers check before filing the ITR? 
Surana advised taxpayers to reconcile their audited financial statements, tax audit report, tax computation and ITR schedules before submitting the return. They should pay particular attention to statutory disallowances, depreciation, deductions, brought-forward losses and tax credits.
 TDS, TCS and advance-tax credits should also be checked against Form 26AS, the Annual Information Statement (AIS) and the books of account.
 If the accounts or tax computation change materially after the audit report has been filed, taxpayers should examine whether the report needs to be revised. A final review by both the taxpayer and the tax auditor can help identify inconsistencies before the ITR is submitted.
